articles.title: Would You Fight a Robot?
articles.description: A human being just fought an actual robot, and Chael Sonnen has questions. Forget the expression “he fights like a robot.” This was metal versus human inside a cage, complete with a crowd, a promoter, and a robot capable of throwing front kicks while maintaining its balance. Chael breaks down why the technology itself is impressive, why robot-versus-robot competition seems inevitable, and why putting a human being across from one creates an entirely different problem. What happens when the robot isn’t programmed to take it easy? What exactly are we trying to prove? And then there’s the question Chael can’t avoid: would he fight one himself? From R2-D2 to Elon Musk’s walking robots to Chael thanking Alexa for ordering his dog food, this one goes places. articles.title: How Did ANY Judge Score This for Pantoja?
articles.description: Joshua Van defeated Alexandre Pantoja again, but Chael Sonnen has one major question: how did any judge score that fight for Pantoja? Chael explains why the result goes beyond what happened on fight night. Pantoja was coming off a real injury and, no matter how disciplined an athlete is during recovery, you don't get better at MMA by being unable to practice MMA. Meanwhile, Van stayed active, went through additional training camps, made weight, competed, and had the opportunity to continue improving. Chael uses Georges St-Pierre, Conor McGregor and NCAA champion Mark Branch to explain the difference between time away and time lost because of injury, and why confidence can only take an athlete so far without the physical work behind it. Pantoja fought like a warrior, but Chael believes Van clearly deserved the decision. And that leaves one question: what exactly did the judge who scored it for Pantoja see? articles.title: Chael’s Advice to Gable Steveson
articles.description: For a limited time only, new customers get 20% off + free shipping at https://blueprint.bryanjohnson.com by using code CHAEL at checkout. #Blueprint #ad Gable Steveson getting caught isn't what concerns Chael Sonnen. The lesson is what Gable does next. Chael explains why elite wrestlers entering MMA often make the same mistake: they hear that they need to become "well-rounded," develop their striking, and then become determined to prove those new skills inside the cage. In the process, they can abandon the enormous advantage that got them there in the first place. Jon Jones is one of the most unique fighters the sport has ever seen. But if he studies the loss and concludes that he needs to become a better striker, Chael believes he'll have learned the wrong lesson. articles.title: This Day in MMA: Jones vs. Gustafsson: The Night Toronto Booed the Decision | Sept. 21
articles.description: September 21, 2013 — Jon Jones and Alexander Gustafsson delivered one of the greatest championship fights in UFC history at UFC 165 in Toronto. Gustafsson became the first fighter to take Jones down and pushed the champion through five brutal rounds. Jones rallied with a pivotal spinning elbow in Round 4 and retained his title by unanimous decision: 48–47, 48–47 and 49–46. The Toronto crowd booed the decision. Jones left on a stretcher, and both fighters were taken to the hospital. The Fight of the Night classic entered the UFC Hall of Fame’s Fight Wing in 2021. This reel features Dana White discussing how close the doctor came to stopping the fight, Jones during the 2013 pre-fight call and both fighters after their 2018 rematch. articles.title: Chael Reacts to Gable Steveson’s KO Loss
articles.description: Visit http://bearmattress.com/chael and use my CODE: chael to get 40% off your Bear mattress! Thank you to Bear Mattress for sponsoring! The reaction to Gable Steveson’s loss tells Chael Sonnen a lot about how long someone has been watching combat sports. One loss does not mean Gable is finished. History is filled with elite fighters who suffered setbacks and came back better. For Chael, the more interesting question is what Gable should take from the experience. Gable entered MMA as one of the hottest prospects the sport has ever seen, with an elite wrestling résumé and expectations unlike almost anyone before him. But there’s a trap that great wrestlers can fall into when transitioning to MMA: believing they need to prove how well-rounded they’ve become. Chael argues they don’t. Your best weapon should remain your priority. Close the distance. Get your hands on your opponent. Put him against the fence. Take him down. If he gets back up, do it again. The striking, submissions, and other skills are there when you need them, but you don’t need to showcase everything you learned in the gym. Sometimes the lesson is much simpler: do what made you great. articles.description: Michael Bisping reacts to Ciryl Gane vs Josh Hokit for the undisputed heavyweight championship at UFC 334 in Madison Square Garden. articles.title: What Exactly Is Ciryl Gane Right Now?
articles.description: Tom Aspinall has vacated the UFC heavyweight championship, but somehow Ciryl Gane isn't automatically the undisputed champion. So what exactly is he? articles.title: Joshua Van vs Alexandre Pantoja 2 #ufc
articles.description: Was Joshua Van’s win over Alexandre Pantoja really a fluke? Chael Sonnen breaks down the story surrounding a potential Pantoja vs. Van rematch—and why the timing could matter just as much as the result. Pantoja has reportedly grown frustrated with the idea of Joshua Van calling himself champion, but Van has taken a very different approach, openly acknowledging that he believes he needs to beat Pantoja again for it to truly mean something. That sets up a fascinating question: who was actually better that night? Chael also examines the biggest variable heading into another fight—the injury Pantoja suffered and how long he has had to recover. If Pantoja only returned to training relatively recently, could that affect how prepared he is when the rematch finally happens? The first fight may be history, but the rematch could settle the argument once and for all. #UFC #MMA #JoshuaVan #AlexandrePantoja #Pantoja #ChaelSonnen #UFCFlyweight #UFCNews #UFCChampionship

articles.title: Arman Tsarukyan Is Becoming Impossible to Ignore #ufc
articles.description: Is Arman Tsarukyan quietly becoming one of the biggest stars in MMA? Chael Sonnen breaks down why Arman has suddenly become impossible to ignore. He’s ranked No. 1, he doesn’t currently have an MMA fight booked, his food-review content is exploding, and he’s still finding ways to stay in the spotlight—including a newly announced matchup with Uriah Faber. But the real question is whether Tsarukyan has the potential to become the UFC’s next major superstar. Chael points to Arman’s performance against Charles Oliveira and the level of competition he has already handled as evidence that the talent is there. He also compares Arman’s rise with the other names being discussed as the next face of the UFC, including Ilia Topuria, Islam Makhachev and Paddy Pimblett. With Conor McGregor absent from the UFC spotlight, who fills that void? Chael thinks Arman Tsarukyan may already be much more interesting than people realize. #UFC #MMA #ArmanTsarukyan #ChaelSonnen #UFCNews #UFCStar #IslamMakhachev #IliaTopuria #PaddyPimblett

articles.title: Arman Tsarukyan Has ONE Goal: Become UFC Champion #ufc
articles.description: Arman Tsarukyan has one goal—and he isn’t letting anything distract him from it: becoming UFC champion. Chael Sonnen reveals his conversation with Arman about preparing for five rounds, staying active in wrestling and jiu-jitsu, and balancing those competitions with his MMA training. Arman’s answer was simple: no matter how big another match is, he never stops training MMA. That mindset is what makes Tsarukyan different. Wrestling and jiu-jitsu aren’t competing with his MMA career—they’re part of the preparation for it. Arman isn’t focused on collecting accomplishments outside the UFC. He wants the UFC lightweight championship, and everything he does is ultimately pointed toward that goal. Chael breaks down why that kind of singular focus can separate an elite fighter from everyone else. #UFC #MMA #ArmanTsarukyan #ChaelSonnen #UFCChampion #UFCNews #UFCTraining #Wrestling #JiuJitsu
